title: IG-CRM: Area/Energy-Efficient IGZO-Based Circuits and Architecture Design for Reconfigurable CIM/CAM Applications
problem: Designing efficient CIM/CAM circuits that support both multiply-accumulate and content search operations for AI workloads. Current SRAM-based approaches suffer from high area and energy overhead.
motivation: IGZO transistors offer ultra-low leakage with >300s data retention and high-density BEOL fabrication, enabling efficient reconfigurable CIM/CAM circuits across diverse AI algorithms.
method: IG-CRM combines a hierarchical circuit design with IGZO transistors (a power-efficient semiconductor material). At the cell level, 3T0C or 4T0C cells (configurations with 3 or 4 transistors and no capacitors) enable both CIM operations (multiply-accumulate calculations for neural networks) and CAM operations (pattern-based content searching). At higher levels, IGZO transistors placed in back-end wiring layers reduce adder tree area (circuits that sum numbers together), and reconfigurable macro-based modules—multiple swappable circuit structures—allow the same chip to handle different AI workloads: deep neural networks, transformers, recommendation systems, and graph neural networks.
key_novelty: IG-CRM's reconfigurable IGZO-based design lets a single chip perform both multiply-accumulate operations (CIM, used in neural networks) and content searching (CAM, used to find data by pattern matching) efficiently across diverse AI tasks.
contributions: First IGZO-based circuits and architecture for reconfigurable CIM/CAM applications
IGZO-based 3T0C/4T0C cell design matching IGZO/CMOS voltage for dual CIM/CAM functionality
Circuit-level area optimization using BEOL IGZO transistors for adder tree reduction
Reconfigurable CIM/CAM architecture supporting DNN, Transformer, RecSys, and GCN applications
primary_theme: IGZO-based reconfigurable CIM/CAM for AI acceleration
